Title: Adding your API keys · Ayumitra help
URL: https://ayumitra.app/help/api-keys.html

[Home](https://ayumitra.app/index.md) Help

# Adding your API keys

On a phone that can run its on-device AI, Ayumitra works fully without any keys. Keys are optional: built-in web search needs none, a search key finds wider, fresher results, and the others let you use a cloud model of your choice.

**Your keys stay on your phone.** They’re kept in the phone’s secure storage and are never sent to Ayumitra. Saving a key sends nothing; it’s only used when you choose web search or a cloud model. You pay the provider directly.

## Which key do you need?

[**Brave Search** Web search for general questions
]
[**Tavily** Web search, with a free plan
]
[**OpenAI** GPT models
]
[**Anthropic** Claude models
]
[**Google Gemini** Gemini models
]
[**OpenRouter** Many models, including free ones
]

## Wider web search with Brave Search or Tavily

Ayumitra can look up general health information online, such as “what is ferritin”. Built-in search does this without a key, with MedlinePlus and Wikipedia, once you turn it on in Settings › Looking things up. A key for Brave Search or Tavily searches the wider web and finds fresher results; the key saved last is the one that searches. Only general, public questions are sent. Your reports, names and conversations stay on your phone. Web search doesn’t need cloud AI.

### Get a key

Either one works. For **Brave Search**, sign up for the [Brave Search API](https://brave.com/search/api/), choose a plan and copy your key from the dashboard. For **Tavily**, sign up at [app.tavily.com](https://app.tavily.com/home), which has a free plan, and copy your key. Tavily says it may keep the questions it receives to improve its search.

### Open Looking things up

In Ayumitra, open **Settings** and find **Looking things up**. Tap **Add** next to **Brave Search** or **Tavily**.

### Paste and save

Paste the key into **API key** and tap **Save key**. You’ll see “Tavily key saved. Web search uses it now.”

### Check it’s on

It now says **On · searches with your Tavily key** (or your Brave Search key). Ayumitra searches on its own when a question needs it. With both keys saved, the one saved last searches; tap the circle beside the other to switch.

## Use a cloud model of your choice

By default, every answer and every report is handled on your phone. If you’d like a larger model, add a key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or OpenRouter. Cloud stays off until you turn it on.

- Provider | Good for | Where to get a key

- OpenAI | GPT models | [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys) › API keys

- Anthropic | Claude models | [platform.claude.com](https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys) › API keys

- Google Gemini | Gemini models | [aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey) › Get API key

- OpenRouter | Many models, including free ones | [openrouter.ai](https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys) › Keys

### Open Cloud AI

Open **Settings**, then **Cloud AI**.

### Save the key

Choose the company, tap **Add key**, paste the key and tap **Save key**. Saving a key sends nothing and turns nothing on.

### Read the agreement

Tap **Read the agreement and turn on**. Cloud AI turns on only once you agree; it covers each company, and a free model asks for one more agreement first.

### Pick your model

In a chat, tap **On this device · Gemma 4** at the top and pick your cloud model. For reports, pick it under **Read reports and photos with** when you add one. You can switch back at any time.

**Privacy shield.** With it on, the names of the people in your profiles, and common other spellings of them, are swapped for made-up ones on your phone before text goes to a cloud model, and swapped back in replies. Nicknames and other people’s names aren’t changed, and names printed on page images can’t be.

**What a cloud model receives.** Chat sends your messages and the health details that matter for the question. Reading a report also sends page images and extracted text. The provider’s charges and retention policies apply. With OpenRouter, free models may keep or learn from what you send, so a paid model is the safer choice for health details. With Google, use a key from a project with billing set up: with a free-tier key, Google may use what you send to improve its products and its reviewers may read it.

## Replace or remove a key

A saved key shows **Saved on this device**, with **Replace** to paste a new one and **Remove**. AI companies’ keys are in **Settings › Cloud AI**; removing one takes chat and reading back to this device. Brave Search and Tavily are under **Settings › Looking things up**; removing the one in use hands searching to the other, and removing both goes back to built-in search.

## Questions

Do I need any key to use Ayumitra?

No, on a phone or tablet that can run the on-device AI (an Android phone with 8 GB of memory, or an iPhone or iPad with 6 GB): reading reports, search, answers, medicines and vaccines all work there without a key. On other devices everything but answers and report reading works without a key; those need a cloud model with your own key.

Does saving a key send my health data anywhere?

No. Saving a key sends nothing. Data is only sent when you choose a cloud model, after a one-time notice, or when web search sends a general question.

Who do I pay?

The provider whose key you use, on their pricing. Ayumitra doesn’t add a charge.

Something isn’t working

Check the key was copied in full, and that your provider account has an active plan or credit. If a cloud request fails, Ayumitra stops and tells you; it never switches provider by itself.

# Vaccination schedules by country

The childhood vaccination schedules Ayumitra follows, for 25 countries, by age. Each page names who publishes the schedule and links its sources.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## South Asia

- [India — IAP-ACVIP Recommended Immunization Schedule (2025), 0–18 years · Universal Immunization Programme: National Immunization Schedule](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/india.md)

- [Nepal — National Immunization Programme: routine schedule (Nepal)](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/nepal.md)

## Southeast Asia

- [Thailand — Thailand EPI](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/thailand.md)
- [Malaysia — Malaysia NIP](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/malaysia.md)
- [Singapore — Singapore NCIS](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/singapore.md)

- [Philippines — Philippines: National Immunization Program (DOH)](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/philippines.md)
- [Vietnam — Vietnam: Chương trình Tiêm chủng mở rộng (EPI)](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/vietnam.md)

## Europe

- [Germany — Germany STIKO](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/germany.md)

Title: India vaccination schedule (2026) · Ayumitra
URL: https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/india.html

[Home](https://ayumitra.app/index.md) [Vaccination schedules](https://ayumitra.app/vaccines/index.md) India

# Vaccination schedule in India (2026)

Two childhood vaccination schedules for India by age: from Indian Academy of Pediatrics, Advisory Committee on Vaccines and Immunization Practices and from Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India ([sources]). In Ayumitra you choose one for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## IAP-ACVIP Recommended Immunization Schedule (2025), 0–18 years

**Published by**
Indian Academy of Pediatrics, Advisory Committee on Vaccines and Immunization Practices

**Version**
2025 recommendations, finalized 22–23 November 2025; published online 9 April 2026 in Indian Pediatrics 2026;63:311–324 (Table 2 and Figure 1)

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | BCG; Oral polio (OPV), birth dose; Hepatitis B, birth dose

- At 6 weeks | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Hepatitis B, dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1

- At 10 weeks | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2; Hib, dose 2; Hepatitis B, dose 3; Rotavirus, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2

- At 14 weeks | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 3; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 3; Hib, dose 3; Hepatitis B, dose 4 (permitted, not required) · optional; Rotavirus, dose 3 (not needed for RV1) · depends on the vaccine used; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 3

- At 6 months | Influenza, dose 1; Typhoid conjugate (TCV) · recommended up to 9 months

- At 7 months | Influenza, dose 2

- At 9 months | MMR, dose 1

- At 12 months | Hepatitis A, dose 1

- At 15 months | MMR, dose 2; Chickenpox (varicella), dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), booster

- At 16 months | DTP, booster 1 · recommended up to 18 months; Hib, booster · recommended up to 18 months; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 1 · recommended up to 18 months

- At 18 months | Hepatitis A, dose 2 (inactivated vaccine only) · depends on the vaccine used · recommended up to 19 months; Chickenpox (varicella), dose 2 · recommended up to 19 months

- At 4 years | DTP, booster 2 · recommended up to 6 years; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 2 · recommended up to 6 years; MMR, dose 3 · recommended up to 6 years

- At 9 years | HPV, dose 1 · recommended up to 15 years

- After an earlier dose | HPV, dose 2 (boys) · for boys · 6 months after the dose before

- At 10 years | Tdap · recommended up to 12 years

- At 16 years | Td or Tdap · recommended up to 18 years

## Universal Immunization Programme: National Immunization Schedule

**Published by**
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

**Version**
National Immunization Schedule (MoHFW/NHM, undated PDF) with: fIPV third dose at 9 months from 1 January 2023 (MoHFW); PCV nationwide from 29 October 2021 (PIB); HPV for girls aged 14 from 28 February 2026 (PIB). Age-wise schedule cross-checked with the PIB backgrounder of 17 March 2026.

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | BCG; Oral polio (OPV), birth dose; Hepatitis B, birth dose

- At 6 weeks | Oral polio (OPV), dose 1; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1

- At 10 weeks | Oral polio (OPV), dose 2; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 2

- At 14 weeks | Oral polio (OPV), dose 3; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 3; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 3; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2

- At 9 months | MR (measles-rubella), dose 1 · recommended up to 12 months; Japanese encephalitis (JE), dose 1 · only in some areas · recommended up to 12 months; Pneumococcal (PCV), booster · recommended up to 12 months; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 3

- At 16 months | MR (measles-rubella), dose 2 · recommended up to 24 months; Japanese encephalitis (JE), dose 2 · only in some areas · recommended up to 24 months; DPT, booster 1 · recommended up to 24 months; Oral polio (OPV), booster · recommended up to 24 months

- At 5 years | DPT, booster 2 · recommended up to 6 years

- At 10 years | Td (tetanus and adult diphtheria), 10 years

- At 14 years | HPV, single dose (girls aged 14) · for girls · recommended up to 15 years

- At 16 years | Td (tetanus and adult diphtheria), 16 years

# Vaccination schedule in Pakistan (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in Pakistan by age, from Federal Directorate of Immunization, Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, Government of Pakistan ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## Expanded Programme on Immunization: routine schedule (Pakistan)

**Published by**
Federal Directorate of Immunization, Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, Government of Pakistan

**Version**
FDI vaccination schedule chart "Vaccination_Schedule_2023" (epi.gov.pk, archived 18 September 2025) and National Immunization Policy 2022, Annexure I and section 4.11 (catch-up). HPV routine phase-in from WHO Pakistan (16 September 2025) and WHO Immunization Data (2025 schedule). epi.gov.pk was unreachable on 2026-10-18; pages were read from the Internet Archive.

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | BCG; Oral polio (OPV), birth dose; Hepatitis B, birth dose (where offered) · only in some areas

- At 6 weeks | Oral polio (OPV), dose 1; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1

- At 10 weeks | Oral polio (OPV), dose 2; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 2

- At 14 weeks | Oral polio (OPV), dose 3; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 3; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 3; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1

- At 9 months | Typhoid conjugate (TCV); MR (measles-rubella), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2

- At 15 months | MR (measles-rubella), dose 2

- At 4 years | DPT booster (Punjab) · only in some areas · recommended up to 5 years

- At 9 years | HPV, single dose (girls aged 9, where introduced) · for girls · only in some areas · recommended up to 10 years

# Vaccination schedule in Bangladesh (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in Bangladesh by age, from Expanded Programme on Immunization, Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Bangladesh ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## Expanded Programme on Immunization: routine schedule (Bangladesh)

**Published by**
Expanded Programme on Immunization, Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Bangladesh

**Version**
DGHS "EPI Vaccine Schedule" (children's routine schedule, file dated January 2018, posted on dghs.gov.bd December 2024) with: HPV single dose for all girls aged 10 from July 2025 (DGHS EPI letter of 28 July 2025); TCV at 15 months from 1 August 2026 (DGHS EPI notice of July 2026 as reported by BSS, and the Civil Surgeon's Office, Sylhet, notice of 15 July 2026). Cross-checked with WHO Immunization Data (2025 schedule, retrieved 2026-10-18).

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | BCG

- At 6 weeks | Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Oral polio (bOPV), dose 1; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 1

- At 10 weeks | Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2; Oral polio (bOPV), dose 2

- At 14 weeks | Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 3; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 3; Oral polio (bOPV), dose 3; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 2

- At 9 months | MR (measles-rubella), dose 1

- At 15 months | MR (measles-rubella), dose 2; Typhoid conjugate (TCV)

- At 10 years | HPV, single dose (girls aged 10) · for girls · recommended up to 11 years

# Vaccination schedule in Sri Lanka (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in Sri Lanka by age, from Epidemiology Unit, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## National Immunization Programme: schedule (Sri Lanka)

**Published by**
Epidemiology Unit, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka

**Version**
"Updated National Immunization Schedule - 2026" (Epidemiology Unit poster, file last modified 31 March 2026), with fIPV moved to 4 and 9 months as recommended by the National Immunization Summit 2025 (report of 18 August 2025). Cross-checked with WHO Immunization Data (2025 schedule, retrieved 2026-10-18).

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | BCG

- At 2 months | Oral polio (OPV), dose 1; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 1

- At 4 months | Oral polio (OPV), dose 2; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 2; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 1

- At 6 months | Oral polio (OPV), dose 3; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 3; BCG, second dose (only if no scar) · optional

- At 9 months | MMR, dose 1; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 2

- At 12 months | Japanese encephalitis (JE, live), single dose

- At 18 months | Oral polio (OPV), dose 4; DTP, dose 4

- At 3 years | MMR, dose 2

- At 5 years | Oral polio (OPV), dose 5; DT (diphtheria-tetanus), dose 5

- At 10 years | HPV, dose 1 (girls, Grade 6) · for girls

- After an earlier dose | HPV, dose 2 (girls) · for girls · 6 months after the dose before

- At 11 years | aTd (adult tetanus-diphtheria), Grade 7

# Vaccination schedule in Nepal (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in Nepal by age, from Family Welfare Division, Department of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Population, Government of Nepal ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## National Immunization Programme: routine schedule (Nepal)

**Published by**
Family Welfare Division, Department of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Population, Government of Nepal

**Version**
NIP Reference Manual for Health Workers 2079 ("Final Revised 2023", posted by FWD 22 December 2023; schedule pp. 9–10, Delay Schedule p. 11) with: fIPV at 14 weeks and 9 months from 20 Kartik 2079 (FWD letters of November 2022); single-dose HPV for grade 6 girls and out-of-school girls aged 10, routine from FY 2082/83 (HPV Vaccine Service Guideline 2081, December 2024). Cross-checked with WHO Immunization Data (2025 schedule, retrieved 2026-10-18) and the DoHS Annual Health Report 2081/82 (June 2026).

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | BCG

- At 6 weeks | Oral polio (bOPV), dose 1; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV10), dose 1; Rotavirus (Rotarix), dose 1

- At 10 weeks | Oral polio (bOPV), dose 2; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV10), dose 2; Rotavirus (Rotarix), dose 2

- At 14 weeks | Oral polio (bOPV), dose 3; Pentavalent (DTP + Hep B + Hib), dose 3; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 1

- At 9 months | MR (measles-rubella), dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV10), dose 3; Injectable polio (fractional IPV), dose 2

- At 12 months | Japanese encephalitis (JE, live), single dose

- At 15 months | MR (measles-rubella), dose 2; Typhoid conjugate (TCV)

- At 10 years | HPV, single dose (girls, grade 6 or aged 10) · for girls · recommended up to 11 years

# Vaccination schedule in Thailand (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in Thailand by age, from Department of Disease Control (กรมควบคุมโรค), Ministry of Public Health, Thailand ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## Thailand EPI

**Published by**
Department of Disease Control (กรมควบคุมโรค), Ministry of Public Health, Thailand

**Version**
กำหนดการให้วัคซีนตามแผนงานสร้างเสริมภูมิคุ้มกันโรค ปี 2566 (DDC, 2023), with 2 IPV + 3 OPV from 1 July 2023 (EPI Operations Standard 2568), PCV at 2, 4 and 12 months from 2 March 2026 (NHSO announcement No. 11/2569, in force 1 October 2026) and influenza for children 6 months to under 5 years (influenza guideline 2569); as of 18 October 2026

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | BCG; Hepatitis B, birth dose

- At 2 months | DTP (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 1; Hib (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 1; Hepatitis B (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1

- At 4 months | DTP (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 2; Hib (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 2; Hepatitis B (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 3; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2

- At 6 months | DTP (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 3; Hib (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 3; Hepatitis B (DTP-HB-Hib), dose 4; Oral polio (OPV), polio dose 3; Rotavirus, dose 3 (not after Rotarix) · depends on the vaccine used; Influenza, first season dose 1 · recommended up to 5 years

- After an earlier dose | Influenza, first season dose 2 · 4 weeks after the dose before; HPV, dose 2 (girls) · for girls · 6 months after the dose before

- At 9 months | MMR, dose 1 · recommended up to 12 months

- At 12 months | Japanese encephalitis (live JE), dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 3 (booster)

- At 18 months | DTP, dose 4 (booster); Oral polio (OPV), polio dose 4; MMR, dose 2

- At 30 months | Japanese encephalitis (live JE), dose 2

- At 4 years | DTP, dose 5 (booster) · recommended up to 6 years; Oral polio (OPV), polio dose 5 · recommended up to 6 years

- At 10 years | HPV, dose 1 (girls) · for girls · recommended up to 13 years

- At 11 years | dT (tetanus and adult-type diphtheria) · recommended up to 13 years

Last checked 18 October 2026.

## Vietnam: Chương trình Tiêm chủng mở rộng (EPI)

**Published by**
Bộ Y tế (Ministry of Health), Viet Nam; Cục Phòng bệnh

**Version**
Thông tư 52/2025/TT-BYT ban hành danh mục bệnh truyền nhiễm, đối tượng và phạm vi phải sử dụng vắc xin, sinh phẩm y tế bắt buộc (31 December 2025; in force 15 February 2026; replaces Thông tư 10/2024/TT-BYT), Điều 1 and Điều 3; month ages of doses 2–3 from the schedule Viet Nam reported to WHO for 2025 (WHO Immunization Data portal, data committed 6 July 2026)

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | Hepatitis B, birth dose; BCG · recommended up to 1 month

- At 2 months | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Hepatitis B, dose 1; Oral polio (OPV), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1 · only in some areas

- At 5 months | Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1

- At 9 months | Measles, dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2

- At 1 year | Japanese encephalitis (JE), dose 1

- At 18 months | DTP, booster 1; MR (measles-rubella)

- At 2 years | Japanese encephalitis (JE), dose 3

- At 7 years | Td (tetanus and reduced diphtheria), booster 2

## Switzerland BAG/EKIF

**Published by**
Bundesamt für Gesundheit (BAG) and Eidgenössische Kommission für Impffragen (EKIF)

**Version**
Schweizerischer Impfplan 2026, Stand Februar 2026 (published 23 February 2026; corrected version 16 April 2026), Table 1 "Synopsis" and chapters 1–3

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At 2 months | DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Hepatitis B, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1 (complementary) · optional

- At 3 months | Meningococcal B (MenB), dose 1 (complementary) · optional

- At 4 months | DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2; Hib, dose 2; Hepatitis B, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 2 (complementary) · optional

- After an earlier dose | Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE), dose 2 (risk areas) · only in some areas · 1 month after the dose before; Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE), dose 3 (risk areas) · only in some areas · 6 months after the dose before; Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE), booster (risk areas) · only in some areas · 10 years after the dose before; HPV, dose 2 · 6 months after the dose before

- At 4 years | DTaP-IPV booster (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis) · recommended up to 7 years; Injectable polio (IPV), booster · recommended up to 7 years

- At 11 years | Tdap booster (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis) · recommended up to 15 years; HPV, dose 1 · recommended up to 14 years; Meningococcal ACWY, adolescent (complementary) · optional · recommended up to 15 years; Meningococcal B (MenB), adolescent dose 1 (complementary) · optional · recommended up to 15 years; Meningococcal B (MenB), adolescent dose 2 (complementary) · optional · recommended up to 15 years

## Belgium SHC (CSS/HGR)

**Published by**
Conseil Supérieur de la Santé / Hoge Gezondheidsraad (Superior Health Council of Belgium); carried out by the Flemish Community (Departement Zorg, Kind en Gezin) and the Wallonia-Brussels Federation (ONE)

**Version**
Advice 9761 "Calendrier vaccinal de base (2025)", validated 3 December 2025, published April 2026 (annex calendar); community calendars: Flanders "Basisvaccinatieschema voor kinderen" (2026), Wallonia-Brussels "Calendrier de vaccination 2025-2026" and "2026-2027" (from 1 November 2026)

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At 8 weeks | DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Hepatitis B, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1

- At 12 weeks | Rotavirus, dose 2

- At 16 weeks | DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2; Hib, dose 2; Hepatitis B, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 3 (3-dose vaccine only) · depends on the vaccine used

- At 12 months | DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 3; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 3; Hib, dose 3; Hepatitis B, dose 3; MMR, dose 1

- At 13 months | Pneumococcal (PCV), booster · recommended up to 15 months; Meningococcal ACWY, small child · recommended up to 15 months

- At 5 years | DTaP-IPV booster (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis) · recommended up to 6 years; Injectable polio (IPV), booster · recommended up to 6 years

- At 7 years | MMR, dose 2 · recommended up to 9 years

- At 11 years | HPV, dose 1 · recommended up to 13 years

- After an earlier dose | HPV, dose 2 · 6 months after the dose before

- At 15 years | Tdap booster (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis) · recommended up to 16 years; Meningococcal ACWY, adolescent · recommended up to 16 years

# Vaccination schedule in the United Kingdom (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in the United Kingdom by age, from UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and NHS England, on the advice of the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI) ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## UK NHS

**Published by**
UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and NHS England, on the advice of the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI)

**Version**
Complete routine immunisation schedule from 1 September 2026 (UKHSA, updated 24 September 2026); children born on or after 1 January 2025

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At 8 weeks | DTaP (6-in-1), dose 1; Injectable polio (6-in-1), dose 1; Hib (6-in-1), dose 1; Hepatitis B (6-in-1), dose 1; Meningococcal B, dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1

- At 12 weeks | DTaP (6-in-1), dose 2; Injectable polio (6-in-1), dose 2; Hib (6-in-1), dose 2; Hepatitis B (6-in-1), dose 2; Meningococcal B, dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 2

- At 16 weeks | DTaP (6-in-1), dose 3; Injectable polio (6-in-1), dose 3; Hib (6-in-1), dose 3; Hepatitis B (6-in-1), dose 3; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1

- At 1 year | Pneumococcal (PCV), booster; Meningococcal B, booster; MMR (as MMRV), dose 1; Chickenpox (as MMRV), dose 1

- At 18 months | DTaP (6-in-1), dose 4; Injectable polio (6-in-1), dose 4; Hib (6-in-1), booster; Hepatitis B (6-in-1), dose 4; MMR (as MMRV), dose 2; Chickenpox (as MMRV), dose 2

- At 40 months | DTaP pre-school booster (4-in-1); Polio pre-school booster (4-in-1)

- At 12 years | HPV, single dose · recommended up to 14 years

- At 14 years | Td teenage booster (3-in-1) · recommended up to 15 years; Polio teenage booster (3-in-1) · recommended up to 15 years; Meningococcal ACWY · recommended up to 15 years

# Vaccination schedule in France (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in France by age, from Ministère chargé de la santé (France), after the opinion of the Haute Autorité de santé ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## Calendrier des vaccinations 2026 (France): enfants et adolescents

**Published by**
Ministère chargé de la santé (France), after the opinion of the Haute Autorité de santé

**Version**
Calendrier des vaccinations et recommandations vaccinales 2026, July 2026 edition (93 pages; file 2026_07_calendrier_vaccinal-2026_a4_93p_v11.pdf): tableau 4.1, section 2 chapters and catch-up tableau 4.5.1

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | RSV antibody (nirsevimab), first RSV season · optional

- At 2 months | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Hepatitis B, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1

- At 3 months | Rotavirus, dose 2; Meningococcal B (MenB), dose 1

- At 4 months | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2; Hib, dose 2; Hepatitis B, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2; Rotavirus, dose 3 (RotaTeq only) · depends on the vaccine used

- At 5 months | Meningococcal B (MenB), dose 2

- At 6 months | Meningococcal ACWY, dose 1

- At 11 months | DTP, booster 1; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 1; Hib, booster; Hepatitis B, dose 3; Pneumococcal (PCV), booster

- At 12 months | MMR, dose 1; Meningococcal B (MenB), booster · recommended up to 15 months; Meningococcal ACWY, dose 2

- At 16 months | MMR, dose 2 · recommended up to 18 months

- At 6 years | DTP, booster 2; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 2

- At 11 years | DTP, booster 3 (reduced-dose dTcaP) · recommended up to 13 years; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 3 · recommended up to 13 years; HPV, dose 1 · recommended up to 15 years; Meningococcal ACWY, adolescent dose · recommended up to 15 years

- After an earlier dose | HPV, dose 2 · 5 months after the dose before

# Vaccination schedule in Italy (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in Italy by age, from Ministero della Salute (Italy); Intesa Governo, Regioni e Province autonome ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## Calendario nazionale vaccinale, PNPV 2023–2025 (Italy): children and adolescents

**Published by**
Ministero della Salute (Italy); Intesa Governo, Regioni e Province autonome

**Version**
Calendario nazionale vaccinale, Intesa Rep. atti n. 193/CSR of 2 August 2023 (G.U. Serie Generale n. 194, 21 August 2023, pp. 62–65). PNPV 2023–2025 extended to 31 December 2026 by Intesa Rep. atti n. 243/CSR of 18 December 2025; no newer national calendar found on 18 October 2026.

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At 2 months | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Hepatitis B, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1 · recommended up to 5 months; Rotavirus, dose 2 · recommended up to 5 months; Rotavirus, dose 3 (three-dose vaccine only) · depends on the vaccine used · recommended up to 5 months

- At 3 months | Meningococcal B (MenB), dose 1

- At 4 months | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2; Hib, dose 2; Hepatitis B, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2

- At 5 months | Meningococcal B (MenB), dose 2

- At 10 months | DTP, booster 1; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 1; Hib, booster; Hepatitis B, dose 3; Pneumococcal (PCV), booster

- At 12 months | MMR, dose 1; Chickenpox (varicella), dose 1; Meningococcal ACWY

- At 13 months | Meningococcal B (MenB), booster · recommended up to 15 months

- At 5 years | DTP, booster 2; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 2; MMR, dose 2; Chickenpox (varicella), dose 2

- At 11 years | HPV, dose 1

- After an earlier dose | HPV, dose 2 · 6 months after the dose before

- At 12 years | DTP, booster 3 (adult-type dTaP) · recommended up to 18 years; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 3 · recommended up to 18 years; Meningococcal ACWY, adolescent dose · recommended up to 18 years

# Vaccination schedule in Spain (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in Spain by age, from Consejo Interterritorial del Sistema Nacional de Salud; Ministerio de Sanidad (Spain) ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## Calendario común de vacunación e inmunización 2026 (Spain): children and adolescents

**Published by**
Consejo Interterritorial del Sistema Nacional de Salud; Ministerio de Sanidad (Spain)

**Version**
Calendario común de vacunación e inmunización a lo largo de toda la vida, calendario recomendado año 2026, approved by the CISNS on 12 December 2025 (PDF dated December 2025). Rotavirus product details from the Ministry's "Recomendaciones de vacunación frente a rotavirus" (approved 18 January 2024, updated 29 February 2024).

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | RSV antibody (nirsevimab), first RSV season · optional

- At 2 months | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Hepatitis B, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Meningococcal B (MenB), dose 1; Rotavirus, dose 1 · recommended up to 6 months; Rotavirus, dose 2 · recommended up to 6 months; Rotavirus, dose 3 (RV5 courses only) · depends on the vaccine used · recommended up to 6 months

- At 4 months | DTP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2; Hib, dose 2; Hepatitis B, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2; Meningococcal B (MenB), dose 2; Meningococcal C (MenC), dose 1

- At 11 months | DTP, booster 1; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 1; Hib, booster; Hepatitis B, dose 3; Pneumococcal (PCV), booster

- At 12 months | MMR, dose 1; Meningococcal B (MenB), booster; Meningococcal C (MenC), dose 2

- At 15 months | Chickenpox (varicella), dose 1

- At 3 years | MMR, dose 2 · recommended up to 5 years; Chickenpox (varicella), dose 2 · recommended up to 5 years

- At 6 years | DTP, booster 2; Injectable polio (IPV), booster 2

- At 12 years | HPV, single dose; Meningococcal ACWY, 12 years

- At 14 years | Td (tetanus, diphtheria), 14 years

# Vaccination schedule in the United States (2026)

The childhood vaccination schedule in the United States by age, from U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) ([sources]). In Ayumitra you can choose it for each child.

Last checked 18 October 2026.

This page is general information, not medical advice. Follow your child’s doctor and your national vaccination programme.

## USA CDC

**Published by**
U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP)

**Version**
Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule by Age, Recommendations for Ages 18 Years or Younger, United States, 2025 (Addendum updated July 2, 2025); the version on cdc.gov on 18 October 2026

**Last checked**
18 October 2026

- Age | Vaccines

- At birth | Hepatitis B, birth dose

- At 1 month | Hepatitis B, dose 2 · recommended up to 2 months

- At 2 months | Rotavirus, dose 1; DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 1; Hib, dose 1; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 1; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 1

- At 4 months | Rotavirus, dose 2; DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 2; Hib, dose 2; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 2; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 2

- At 6 months | Hepatitis B, dose 3 · recommended up to 18 months; Rotavirus, dose 3 (RotaTeq only) · depends on the vaccine used; DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), dose 3; Hib, dose 3 (not needed after PedvaxHIB) · depends on the vaccine used; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 3; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 3 · recommended up to 18 months; Influenza, first season dose 1

- After an earlier dose | Influenza, first season dose 2 (under 9 years) · 4 weeks after the dose before; HPV, dose 2 · 6 months after the dose before; Meningococcal B, dose 2 (shared decision) · optional · 6 months after the dose before

- At 12 months | Hib, booster · recommended up to 15 months; Pneumococcal (PCV), dose 4 · recommended up to 15 months; MMR, dose 1 · recommended up to 15 months; Chickenpox (varicella), dose 1 · recommended up to 15 months; Hepatitis A, dose 1 · recommended up to 23 months

- At 15 months | DTaP, dose 4 (booster) · recommended up to 18 months

- At 18 months | Hepatitis A, dose 2 · recommended up to 23 months

- At 4 years | DTaP, dose 5 (booster) · recommended up to 6 years; Injectable polio (IPV), dose 4 · recommended up to 6 years; MMR, dose 2 · recommended up to 6 years; Chickenpox (varicella), dose 2 · recommended up to 6 years

- At 11 years | Tdap (adolescent booster) · recommended up to 12 years; HPV, dose 1 · recommended up to 12 years; Meningococcal ACWY, dose 1 · recommended up to 12 years

- At 16 years | Meningococcal ACWY, dose 2 (booster); Meningococcal B, dose 1 (shared decision) · optional · recommended up to 18 years
